reviews.comment: Great professor! This class was easy to follow if you the work was put in. Really helpful during office hours, he wants to help! Studied a few hours every few days a week and got As on all his exams. Lab is difficult however lecture is definitely manageable. Extra credit is given!
reviews.ratingTags: EXTRA CREDIT--Gives good feedback--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: Definitely take him for Ochem, he's such a great professor, and you will make an A if you do the in-class and ask him/TAs for help.
reviews.ratingTags: EXTRA CREDIT--Gives good feedback--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: If you see him for o chem take him. Daily in class worksheets to get you practicing the material straight away. He has IA,s walk around to help you and he stays after class to help you as well. Great professor all around and the exam have bonus integrated with it so you can score a perfect score without even doing everything right. TAKE HIM TRUST!
reviews.ratingTags: EXTRA CREDIT--Gives good feedback--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: Provides lots of practice problems and lets students learn from their mistakes. Extra credit for submitting in-class assignments. Gave helpful feedback during office hours and problem sessions. This is a hands-on course. Guess, get it wrong, ask questions,  try again = A+ (even if you're a bad test-taker or are slow to grasp some concepts)

Despite what everyone says about Dr. Singleton and his teaching methods, he's honestly pretty great. His lectures tend to be a bit boring and sometimes it's hard to understand what he's saying (he wouldn't use a microphone.) But overall, his work is straightforward and if you are confused, HE WILL WORK WITH YOU, and give you resources.

Easiest organic chemistry class! Finish the in-class assignments with the TAs and Dr. Singleton to get up to 20 bonus points on each Exam. Exams have additional bonus points embedded into them and are very similar to the given practice problems and the in-class assignments. I recommend reading his notes and practicing often. Many 100s on exams!

Dr. Singleton is a very misunderstood professor because he clearly has character. Still, to me, he is one of the funniest professors I have ever had (do not take him too seriously, I guarantee he is not serious). As someone who hated general chemistry, he makes organic chemistry incredibly easy! It is important to put a lot of time and effort.

DAS is amazing. A LOT of extra cred (+1 pt daily hw and built-in pts for test) High grade distribution. Weekly problem session = great practice for test (unlike old exam problems bc no key given) He makes notes but you must *annotate* in lecture to learn. Fun personality. Annotate in class + attend most sessions = pretty easy A. Take honors for him

This is by far the worst professor I have ever had. I warn all my friends to STAY AWAY. Lectures too fast and jumps around a lot, gives notes but they're hard to understand, wants us to know everything in txtbk but also tells us that it's wrong all the time. Only gives extra credit if you get certain problems right (hurts those who rly need it).

I took honors and I will say it is difficult and requires a lot of time outside of class, but Dr. Singleton is a great professor and is very accessible outside of class. Office hours pretty much every day and hold reviews before the exams. Tough grader but lots of EC. He understands the material is difficult but truly wants you to succeed.

Please, save yourself and do not take him. He goes off the textbook a lot, but also wants you to know everything from the textbook. Claims to know "better" than the txtbook, which makes the fact that you basically have to teach yourself pretty difficult. He mostly lectures and walked around "grading" our reactions and mechanisms. Not helpful at all

Best chemistry professor for people that actually care about learning the material. You can read the assigned readings before class and the lecture notes that he does clean up any questions you might have. He's very willing to answer any questions students may have and hosts many review sessions to ensure all students have a chance to succeed.

There is a worksheet each lecture that you can turn in to get extra credit. The grading is lenient, so just turn it in with something to get pts. I had to teach myself ochem because his lectures+ notes were confusing. He has study sessions and tons of TAs to help. Hard class/ takes a lot of personal effort- this class is NOT for the weak lol.

He was chosen as a sub for my class then shortly became our full time professor. He is disrespectful and demeaning to students. He doesn't give real feedback (he gives it in the form of yes or no) and lectures insanely fast (except when he's talking about his research). Do yourself a favor, avoid him

Hard class, but Dr. Singleton makes it worthwhile. There are optional worksheets that let you practice lecture material while in class and gets you bonus points on homework. 4 tests, with extra bonus points on each one, and extensive study sessions. It's a different way of teaching from other professors, but just as good.

Dr. Singleton was amazing - lots of review sessions outside of class & very understanding. Provides lots of feedback & typically has extra points available on exams. The average grade at the end of the semester was an A. Can get super sidetracked during lectures but very personable, likeable, & respectable. Loved having him.
Did not adapt to COVID teaching very well, lectures and pre-made notes were not very engaging

Very bad his lectures are extremely confusing and do not make sense. Now I am in lab with the non majors (Chem 238) and made an A. The actual lab is ok but the lecture portion is difficult and he made it more difficult than it needed to be. I learned everything he was supposed to teach in chem 228. So glad Im not a chem major anymore.
reviews.ratingTags: Lots of homework--Skip class? You won't pass.

reviews.comment: I learned more about how much money he makes using the techniques mentioned in lecture compared to ACTUALLY LEARNING the techniques. Even when he tries to lecture, I wouldn't understand 99.99% of the things he says and just zone out for the rest of lecture. 10/10 do not recommend.

Assigns weekly homework that requires you to play "Where's Waldo" with the incoherent packets he hands out to find the correct information / equations, and he'll still mark you down. Nobody knows how to study for the tests; in fact, nobody knows what we're learning. Avoid.

Worst chem prof at TAMU. Hands out tons of papers and problem sets and doesn't teach the content on the sets. Has an "outline" of his notes but they don't help at all and leave you with lots of questions. Avoid.
reviews.ratingTags: Lots of homework--Skip class? You won't pass.--Tough grader

reviews.comment: Honestly amazing professor and a skilled lecturer. Doesn't follow the book so focus on lecture notes. Tons of practice problems and weekly review sessions. His grading system is nonconventional, top X% of class gets an A and if you have above a 90 but are not top X%, he won't give you an A.

Overall a very good professor for the material. He doesn't like how the book covers some of the material though, so focus on studying lecture notes before exams not homework. Beyond lecture notes, Singleton gave out many review questions. Additionally, the weekly problem sessions were a very nice opportunity to get feedback on working problems.

Dr. Singleton is the greatest professor I have had so far. He made organic chemistry understandable and enjoyable. He holds weekly problem sessions that are great for feedback from him directly, and you get a lot of practice for each chapter. His exams aren't really that hard and have some bonus points built in. Overall a fantastic professor.
reviews.ratingTags: Gives good feedback--Clear grading criteria--Amazing lectures
